title: fxv interrupted-sync error detail
description: Describes a sync, goto, revert, resolve, rollback, branch switch or copy that was interrupted before it finished, leaving the workspace in an inconsistent state. Only ever a detail payload, riding in an error envelope's `error_data` (with `kind` of `interrupted-sync`, alongside exit code 98) when a command refuses to run because of it, or when a command stops on file changes it could not apply, which leaves the same state. `fxv resume` recovers rather than reports, so asking what state a workspace is in is `fxv status`'s job.

oneOf.description: The journal was readable, so the run can be finished with `fxv resume --continue`, or undone with `fxv resume --rollback` when `operation` is not `rollback` and `source_revision` is present.

operation.description: The command that did not finish: it was interrupted, or stopped on file changes it could not apply.

summary.description: A ready-to-display sentence describing what the run was doing, phrased per operation, e.g. "Was syncing from main.11 to main.12."

target_revision.description: Revision spec the interrupted run was moving to, and where a continue finishes.

source_revision.description: Revision spec the workspace is still recorded as synced to, and where a rollback returns to. Absent when the interrupted run was a checkout into a workspace that had never synced.

total_entries.description: File changes in the interrupted run's plan.

preserved_entries.description: Entries whose locally-modified file was moved aside rather than overwritten.

remaining_entries.description: Entries that never reached a terminal state. A continue applies these and the failed entries.

sampled_unfinished_paths.description: A capped sample of the unfinished paths, workspace-relative with '/' separators; `remaining_entries` is the true count.

sampled_failed_paths.description: Since 1.1. A capped sample of the paths whose change could not be applied, each with why; `failed_entries` is the true count.

kind.description: The kind of failure, or null when the journal did not record one (a journal written before kinds were recorded, or one whose run was interrupted while recording it). A minor version may add kinds, so a consumer should treat a kind it does not know as `other`.

message.description: The failure's message. Present only in the error of the command that stopped on the failure, not when a later command reports the journal.

oneOf.description: The journal survived but could not be parsed, so neither recovery operation can act on it.
